2. Learned Advocate for the petitioner after placing the impugned judgment and other materials on record submitted that Labour Court acted illegally in not dismissing the case on the ground of limitation as the respondent No. 2 failed to file the grievance petition within the statutory period and that Labour Court without finding any fault with the enquiry proceedings illegally set aside the dismissal order relying upon evidence adduced before it. 

 7. It has already been noticed that petitioner could not produce before the Labour Court any document to show that dismissal order dated 25-3-88 was sent to the respondent No. 2 by registered post by the petitioner. On the other hand, respondent No. 2 categorically stated in his deposition that he came to know about the same only on 21-5-88 and sent a grievance petition on 24-5-88 by registered post which was refused by the petitioner. Thereafter he filed the case on 9-7-88. In view of the same we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that limitation for filing the case should have been calculated from 25-3-88 and Labour Court acted illegally in not dismissing the case on the ground of limitation.
